newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's ASKO to boost monthly sales by 30-40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russia's ASKO to boost monthly sales by 30-40 pct.

text.p: ASKO, Russia's biggest private insurance company, said on Friday a restructuring programme now in progress will boost its sales by 30 to 40 percent a month this year.

This spring medium-sized Russian bank Suprimexbank bought ASKO and started the restructuring programme, which will be finished by the end of this year, ASKO general manager Alexander Bunishkin told a news conference.
In rouble terms sales will grow by between 1.50 to 2.00 billion roubles a month, Bunishkin said.

Strakhovaya Kompaniya ASKO has cut the number of managers by 80 to 230, cutting costs by 40 percent. It plans to train at least 1,000 agents and has increased its charter capital 25-fold to 49.90 billion roubles, he said.
"We had too many people who did analysis, who counted money, but too few who earned that money," Bunishkin said.
ASKO will concentrate on property and cargo insurance, liability insurance, re-insurance, medical insurance and life assurance, he said.
ASKO will use the funds released by cutting costs to offer discounts to some of its clients, it said in a statement.
ASKO is cutting the cost of property and life insurance for individual policy-holders in the Moscow region by 50 percent, and car insurance by five percent, it said.
Corporate clients will have a 20 percent discount when insuring buildings and equipment, up to five percent discount when insuring cars and up to 20 percent when insuring staff.
